# Independent H.264 pixel fixtures

These streams were generated from synthetic FFmpeg lavfi sources with
`generate.sh`, using FFmpeg 9.0.1 and its libx264 encoder. The companion `.yuv`
files are FFmpeg's independently decoded planar 8-bit YCbCr 4:2:0 output, in
presentation order, with visible cropping applied. They were not generated by
our decoder. No media or codec implementation was copied from another project.

The script records every encoder setting. Re-run from any directory with:

```sh
./test/integration/testdata/h264/generate.sh
```

FFmpeg/libx264 are only needed to regenerate fixtures, not to build the package,
run the broker, or execute the tests. Encoder updates may change the compressed
streams; regenerate the companion references together.

- `intra-*`: one independently coded frame per stream, including flat areas,
  gradients, detailed content, non-macroblock-aligned dimensions, multiple
  slices and varied deblocking settings. `intra-360p` is 640x360; smaller inputs
  keep the correctness suite fast.
- `motion-*` without B/scaling suffixes: 20 pictures per stream, with AUD NALs delimiting complete access
  units and a second IDR during the sequence. These exercise I/P prediction,
  reference lists and entropy modes.
- `motion-b-*`: 30 pictures per stream, covering spatial/temporal direct
  prediction, all CABAC initialization modes, CAVLC, implicit weighting, multiple
  slices and B-pyramid references. Output references are in display order.
- `*-scaling-*`: JVT default and explicit custom scaling matrices, with I/P/B
  pictures and 4x4/8x8 transforms.
- `*-cabac*`: CABAC coding; predictive fixtures include `cabac_init_idc` 0/1/2.
- `*-high-*`: High profile with 8x8 transforms enabled, in both entropy modes.

The test compares every sample, not only hashes, dimensions or JPEG headers.
This is a growing regression corpus, not a conformance certification.
